and punishes licentiousness, hence the Buddha shows karmic retribution, urging people toward goodness and deterring evil.
Heaven and hell are both created by human actions, arising from within the heart-mind. Thus,
those who do good ascend to heaven, while evildoers fall into hell. Loyal ministers,
filial sons, virtuous people, and chaste women—their hearts are Buddha-like, hence divine protection and
eradication of karmic obstacles; thus, in life they do not violate laws, and after death do not fall into the avīci hell.

past accumulated faults then become like a speck of dust in vast space, a snowflake in a red furnace—completely
dissolved and cleansed. Even if retribution were due, how could it take effect? I often reflect on this, fearing that people

such persons have few desires and know contentment,
able to cultivate the practices of Pǔxián.
If after the Thus Come One's nirvāṇa, in the latter five hundred years,
if people see those who accept, uphold, and recite the Lotus Sutra,
'These persons will soon reach the site of enlightenment,
and sit on the lion's seat of the Dharma amid the great assembly of gods and humans.'
If in future ages, there are those who accept, uphold, and recite this sutra,
such persons will no longer crave clothing, bedding, food, drink, or material possessions,
their wishes will not be in vain,
and they will also obtain their karmic rewards in the present life.
If anyone lightly slanders them, saying:
The karmic retribution for such offenses will be blindness life after life.
If there are those who make offerings and praise them,
they will obtain visible rewards in this present life.
If further, upon seeing those who accept and uphold this sutra,
they point out their faults and evils,
such persons will in this present life contract leukoderma.
If anyone lightly laughs at them,
they will life after life have sparse and missing teeth,
ugly lips, flat nose, contorted hands and feet,
dropsy, shortness of breath, and various severe illnesses.
If you see those who accept and uphold this sutra,
you should rise and greet them from afar,
respecting them as you would the Buddha."
When this chapter "Encouragement of Pǔxián" was spoken,
immeasurable, boundless bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges attained the Hundreds of Thousands of Myriads of Kotis Whirling Dhāraṇī;
bodhisattvas as numerous as the dust particles of the three-thousand-great-thousand-worlds perfected the Way of Pǔxián.
When the Buddha preached this sutra,
the Bodhisattva Pǔxián and other bodhisattvas,
and various gods, dragons, humans, non-humans, and others,
the entire great assembly, greatly rejoiced,
accepted and upheld the Buddha's words,
The later Qin dynasty monk Sēng Ruì composed:
The Lotus Sutra is the secret treasury of all buddhas, the true essence of all scriptures. It is named "Flower"
to illuminate its origin; called "Pútuólì" (white lotus) to praise its flourishing. What it
reveals is profound, its principles subtle. Unless transmitted by those with penetrating understanding, few can
find its gateway. Just as the essence of all medicinal herbs and trees lies in their fruits, so the eighty-four
thousand Dharma repositories originate from the fruit of the Way - hence this analogy. Among all
flowers, the lotus stands supreme: unopened buds are called "Jūmóluó"; blossoms about to
fall are named "Jiāmóluó"; while in full glorious bloom, they're termed "Pútuólì". The unopened bud symbolizes the Two
Vehicles, the fading flower represents Nirvana, but only the radiant bloom adequately illustrates this sutra. As for the Prajñā
sutras, their depth reaches ultimate reality, thus practitioners return through them; their breadth
encompasses all, thus vehicles cross by them. Yet their general approach prioritizes adaptive teaching
as paramount; for responding to worldly needs, they necessarily employ skillful means. Though transformative
power through such means enlightens many, they remain insufficient regarding true essence - thus all belong to the Lotus Sutra,
as is fitting. Exploring its profound principles reveals vast grandeur, its coverage extensive - how could it merely
expound reality and return to source, or finalize different paths? It truly illuminates awakening's principle,
embracing past and present. Speaking of the Buddha's immeasurable lifespan, eternity cannot convey its duration;
of countless manifested bodies, myriad forms cannot differentiate their essence. Thus the Life Chapter
establishes transcendence of quantification, the Manifested Bodies chapter clarifies insubstantiality, Samantabhadra reveals non-attainment,
and Prabhūtaratna illuminates non-extinction. Tracing the ancient to this present, ten thousand ages become one
day; comprehending mystery through all transformations, a thousand paths share one track. Thus,
cyclic existence cannot anticipate preservation, while eternal quiescence cannot be called extinction.
Seeking the profound doctrine by rejecting the past loses accomplishment in fundamental emptiness; controlling the mind's reins
through samādhi forgets temporal limits in dual realms. Though this sutra has circulated in our land nearly a century,
translators missed its subtle passages, failing to open its spiritual gates; expositors strayed from its standards,
rarely treading its profound path. White-haired scholars searched in vain,
none glimpsing its gateway. Qín Sīlì Xiàowèi Zuǒ Jiāngjūn Ānchéng Hóu Yáo Sōng,
resonating with metaphysical gates, dwelling beyond worldly concerns, devotedly studied this sutra with profound faith,
constantly pondering its text and deeply recognizing translators' errors. Meeting Kumārajīva Dharma Master,
he requested its transmission. Pointing to its great return to truth was like parting thick clouds to ascend high,
mounting Kūnlún to gaze below. Then over eight hundred monks attended and comprehended,
all distinguished talents from various regions, outstanding contemporaries. This was the eighth year of Hóngshǐ,
Lǔ Guó Tàifūrén Madame Zhāng, humbly encountering
her late husband Grand Tutor and Chancellor Lǐ Gōng's distant memorial day, reverently donated pure wealth of one string
of cash to Fúzhōu Kāiyuán Monastery's Great Canon Bureau, to carve the "phoenix-case" edition of the Seven Volumes
of the Wonderful Dharma Lotus Flower Sutra and the "Lotus Samādhi",
relying on these supreme causes to honor the departed and transcend birth toward the Pure Land. Dated the fifteenth day
of the first month, Shàoxīng era's twenty-first year, reverently inscribed.
